Hi Lisa —

Below is a concise, procurement-ready summary of how we verify service commitments and the guardrails for a temporary exemption. Happy to expand any section.

1) SLO definitions (what we measure)
- Uptime SLO: 99.95% monthly availability for API surface (successful 2xx responses for standard generation endpoints).
- Latency SLOs: p95 and p99 for request->first-byte and request->completion over 1-minute rolling windows. Default latency SLO for interactive models is p95 < 300ms for small prompt size; we provide model-specific baselines in the model catalog.

2) Failure events and measurement methodology
- Failure event: a request returning >=5xx or timeout at the platform ingress. We measure both synthetic probes and real-user telemetry. Final SLO calculations are based on a blended signal where real-user traffic is primary; synthetic probes are used for internal detection and to fill low-traffic windows.
- Measurement window: we compute SLOs on per-minute buckets, aggregated to hourly and monthly windows for reporting. Monthly SLO = (sum of successful minutes)/(total minutes in the month) expressed as percentage.
- Sampling: real-user events are sampled at 100% for success/error counters but traces are sampled (default 1%) to reduce overhead. For customers requesting additional fidelity during a migration, we can temporarily increase sampling to 10% for a 7-day window with prior notice.

3) Alerting and escalation
- Thresholds: immediate pager at >1.0% error rate sustained over 5 minutes, and an SRE runbook triggers at >0.5% sustained over 15 minutes. Latency-based alerts at p99 exceeding configured model baseline by 2x for 5 minutes.
- Notifications: customers can opt into email/SMS for major incidents; we also provide status pages for global incidents.

4) Customer visibility and exports
- Read-only dashboard: we provide a Grafana read-only dashboard (link below) scoped to Acme's tenancy. Dashboards include uptime, error-rate trends, latency percentiles, and per-route breakdowns.
- Raw exports: we can provide a one-time log export for the migration week (JSONL) covering request/response status and latency fields, retained for 30 days by default. Longer retention options are available as a paid add-on.
- Data retention policy: default operational telemetry retained 30 days; aggregated SLO history (monthly aggregates) retained for 13 months.

5) Temporary exemption policy (procurement-ready language)
- Redwood acknowledges Acme's planned migration window and will exclude transient, planned migration-related errors from SLA credit calculations if the following hold: (a) Acme provides a migration start/end time window no less than 48 hours prior to the start; (b) Acme enables the increased sampling flag and accepts read-only Grafana access; (c) Redwood's SRE runbook is on standby for the window.
- Maximum exemption duration: 7 consecutive calendar days per migration event.
- Acceptance criteria: exception applies only to deviations where error rates are driven by traffic cutover (e.g., client-side retries causing spikes). Platform-level outages (complete service unavailability) remain subject to standard SLA terms.

6) Implementation steps for week of migration
- We will provision a read-only Grafana invite for Acme by EOD Fri (https://grafana.redwood.com/d/readonly/acme-visibility?orgId=1).
- Increase telemetry sampling to 10% for the specified 7-day window on request.
- We will provide a raw telemetry export (JSONL) covering the migration week within 48 hours after the window closes.

If that language looks good to procurement, we can add it as an amendment to the SOW. If you prefer, I can convert the temporary exemption policy to a short clause for DocuSign.

- Ben Carter
Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
